s1.syndrome_frame: Painless mass on the frontal bone with a 2-month history and associated radiographic findings
salient_findings: Painless mass on the right side of the frontal bone
Lytic lesion of the frontal bone with a soap-bubble appearance on CT
Lobulated frontal-bone mass with avid enhancement on MRI
key_facts: 50-year-old man
2-month history of a painless mass
Mass located on the right side of the frontal bone
Mass measured approximately 4.0 × 3.5 cm
Mass was well circumscribed, soft, nonmobile, and non-tender
Laboratory studies were unremarkable
Neurologic examination was unremarkable
Plain radiography showed a large, circumscribed radiolucent lesion
CT showed cortical destruction of the inner and outer tables
MRI showed a lobulated mass that was hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Soap-bubble appearance on radiography and lytic lesion with cortical destruction on CT are characteristic of giant cell tumor

shortlist.label: Hemangioma of the bone
shortlist.why_kept: Well-circumscribed radiolucent lesion with a soap-bubble appearance is also seen in hemangiomas

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Painless mass with a well-circumscribed radiolucent lesion could be an osteoma, although the size is larger than typical

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Lobulated mass with fluid-fluid levels on MRI could be an aneurysmal bone cyst, although the clinical presentation is not typical

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Ground-glass appearance on radiography and cortical thinning on CT could be seen in fibrous dysplasia, although the clinical presentation is not typical
